conversations.prompt: Is there much of a difference between the best by and sell by date?
conversations.chosen_response:

The “best-by” date, on the other hand, is a suggestion made by the manufacturer, that you should use the product before that date.  If you follow it, you will almost certainly not have any issues, but it’s not guaranteed.  The food industry is a lot more regulated about how strict the best-by dates need to be, and in the U.S., you can’t sell a product past its “best-by” date unless it passes government tests to make sure it hasn’t gone bad.  There are some online databases you can consult to see whether or not a product can be legally sold past its best-by date, such as https://www.upcdatabase.com/.
